# fluss-go v0.2.0-beta.5

This beta fixes data delivery, physical key encoding, and metadata handling
for Apache Fluss 1.0.0. fluss-go remains pure Go and does not link or wrap
the Apache Fluss Rust Core. The Go baseline remains 1.26.11.

## Upgrade

- Upgrade the root and any HDFS, OSS, OpenTelemetry, or S3 adapters together.
  Apache Fluss 0.9.1 users must remain on fluss-go `v0.1.0-beta.11`.
- `WithBatchLimit` now bounds each KV current-state poll, not the entire
  scan. Process rows returned on the terminal poll before stopping. For a
  persisted KV snapshot, resume log reads at the returned `LogOffset`
  without adding one. For a KV current-state scan, consume every snapshot row
  for the bucket, then use `AtOffset(result.SnapshotLogOffset)` when
  `SnapshotLogOffsetKnown` is true. A missing offset is not zero; querying
  `Latest()` later can skip changes.
- Tables without an explicit log format default to Arrow. Use `AppendArrow`
  with `fgo.Append` changes, or explicitly select COMPACTED or INDEXED when
  creating a table for row appends.
- Review existing partitioned KV keys and wide DECIMAL keys before rollout
  if an older fluss-go wrote the table. Corrected physical keys are not
  migrated automatically. Keyed KV operations on lake-bound tables and
  automatic row routing for keyed lake-bound logs are rejected where safe
  routing is unsupported.

See the [migration guide](https://github.com/pletorco/fluss-go/blob/v0.2.0-beta.5/docs/migration-v0.2.md#upgrading-from-v020-beta4)
and [KV key cutover guidance](https://github.com/pletorco/fluss-go/blob/v0.2.0-beta.5/docs/data-operations.md#kv-key-compatibility).

```sh
go get github.com/pletorco/fluss-go@v0.2.0-beta.5
go get github.com/pletorco/fluss-go/adapters/s3@v0.2.0-beta.5
go mod tidy
```

## Highlights

- Preserve pending scan results across recoverable typed codec failures and
  interrupted KV polls. Bounded log scans also retain server-reported
  filtered progress toward their stopping offsets.
- Return ready log rows without a long wait on an empty peer bucket. Retry
  a stateless log batch read once after leader failover, only on the same
  physical bucket. Established KV scan sessions are never replayed.
- Correct partitioned KV routing, wide DECIMAL key encoding, and log-batch
  framing for Fluss magic 1 and 2. Validate Arrow partition and change-kind
  input before queuing it. Absent write offsets are kept unknown.
- Keep schemas and partition routes tied to the right table identity, even
  after drop and recreation. Prevent abandoned refreshes from overwriting
  newer metadata and honor cancellation while waiting for active polls.
- Honor setup timeouts through TLS, API negotiation, and authentication.
  Preserve completed RPC responses if the peer immediately disconnects and
  keep healthy KV buckets moving while another bucket is throttled.
- Treat revoked filesystem credentials as invalid, renew before their usable
  deadline, and report terminal read errors instead of silently accepting
  incomplete storage data.
- Update Arrow Go to `v18.9.0` and the optional S3 adapter's AWS SDK service
  package to `v1.116.0`.

The [changelog](https://github.com/pletorco/fluss-go/blob/v0.2.0-beta.5/CHANGELOG.md#v020-beta5---2026-11-27)
lists the remaining fixes.

## Known limitations

Apache Fluss 1.0.0 server limitations are not worked around by this beta.
They include partial upserts with a required auto-increment column
([#290](https://github.com/pletorco/fluss-go/issues/290)) and adding a column
with position FIRST ([#321](https://github.com/pletorco/fluss-go/issues/321)).
An absent snapshot lease is not proof that the server pinned a snapshot
([#318](https://github.com/pletorco/fluss-go/issues/318)).
Native Iceberg, Lance, and Paimon planning remains application-owned.

## Verification

Live compatibility targets Apache Fluss `1.0.0` at commit
`5c07f88e50a8ff41b0ebc214a0458e5dba60be37`, with image digest
`sha256:ff461b45438033da4fd1c2556d3f978f3603bb3632fe075c2bd57388339a58cb`.
The release requires unit, race, golden, fuzz-smoke, API, documentation,
security, license, Sonar, live Fluss, and live storage gates.
